## A. Domain Crate Contract Summary

Per [WORKFLOW_TOOLS_DOMAIN_CRATE_CONTRACT.md](WORKFLOW_TOOLS_DOMAIN_CRATE_CONTRACT.md), the canonical (newer, aspirational) shape is:

```
{domain}/crates/{domain}-api/            # internal API crate — types, logic, errors
{domain}/crates/{domain}/                # public facade crate: lib.rs re-exports {domain}-api
  src/bin/{domain}-cli.rs
  src/bin/{domain}-mcp.rs
  src/bin/{domain}-http.rs
```
- The public `{domain}` crate declares `[lib]` + one `[[bin]]` per transport, each gated by a cargo feature (`cli`, `mcp`, `http`) that also gates a shared `transport-harness` dependency (owned by `memory-kernel/crates/transport-harness`; canonical spec lives in the memory-kernel submodule, slug `transport-harness`).
- Executable names stay stable: `{domain}-cli`, `{domain}-mcp`, `{domain}-http`.
- Reference/compiling example: [workflow-tools-contract-reference/crates/](workflow-tools-contract-reference/crates) has `example-api` + `example` (facade with gated bins).

**Important divergence**: this contract is not what most *existing* tool trios in the repo actually use. `peek-api`/`peek-cli`/`peek-mcp` (and the ticket/spec/rule/test/session/audit/feedback/fs family) are three **separate top-level crates**, not one facade crate with feature-gated bins. A new `pdf` trio should decide explicitly which pattern to follow — see Open Questions.

## B. peek Trio Reference Layout (concrete template)

```
memory-api/crates/peek-api/         Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs
memory-api/tools/cli/peek-cli/      Cargo.toml, src/, tests/
memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/      Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, src/server.rs
```

`peek-api` ([Cargo.toml](memory-api/crates/peek-api/Cargo.toml)):
- lib-only crate (`peek_api`), deps: `regex`, `serde`+derive, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `toon-format`; dev-dep `tempfile`.
- [src/lib.rs](memory-api/crates/peek-api/src/lib.rs) defines: `PeekResponse` (serde struct), `InspectRequest`/`InspectMode` (tagged enum: `mode` = snake_case), `PeekRequest` (tagged enum: `kind`), `PeekError` (`thiserror::Error`), a single `execute(&PeekRequest) -> Result<PeekResponse, PeekError>` entry point, plus a `write_output` helper and private implementation functions. This is the request/response/error convention: tagged serde enums for request variants, one dispatch function, `thiserror` for the error enum.

`peek-mcp` ([Cargo.toml](memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/Cargo.toml)):
- Depends on `peek-api` by path, `rmcp` (`server`, `transport-io` features), `serde`/`serde_json`, `tokio` (full), `tracing`+`tracing-subscriber`.
- [src/server.rs](memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/src/server.rs) pattern (concrete, copy-ready):
  - One `#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]` input struct per tool (e.g. `PeekReadInput`, `PeekGrepInput`).
  - A `PeekServer { tool_router: ToolRouter<Self> }` struct with `new()`/`Default`, plus private helpers `json_result<T: Serialize>` (serializes response to `CallToolResult::success`) and an error mapper (`peek_err`) converting the api crate's error enum into `McpError` (`invalid_params` for user errors, `internal_error` for internal ones).
  - `#[tool_router] impl PeekServer { #[tool(name = "...", description = "...")] pub async fn peek_read(&self, Parameters(input): Parameters<PeekReadInput>) -> Result<CallToolResult, McpError> { ... } }` — one method per named tool, each building an api-crate request and calling a shared `run_request` dispatcher.
  - `#[tool_handler] impl ServerHandler for PeekServer` — sets `server_info` from `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"/"CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, a hand-written `instructions` string describing the tool set, and `ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build()`.
  - `pub async fn run_mcp_server()` — constructs server, calls `.serve(stdio())`, awaits `.waiting()`.
- Output bounding/compaction happens **inside `peek-api`**, not the MCP layer: bounded reads (`DEFAULT_WINDOW = 40` lines), skeletonization, and TOON-formatted `repo_map.toon` handling are implemented in [peek-api/src/lib.rs](memory-api/crates/peek-api/src/lib.rs) (`render_window`, `skeletonize*`, `REPO_MAP_FILE` constant). The MCP server is a thin adapter that just serializes the already-bounded response to JSON text.

## C. Recommended Crate Placement + Workspace Edits

The `memory-api/` workspace is where every named-tool domain trio (ticket, spec, rule, test, session, audit, feedback, fs, peek, compact-terminal, doc) already lives, registered in the **root** [Cargo.toml](Cargo.toml) `members` list (not a nested workspace Cargo.toml under `memory-api/`). `context-stack/` is reserved for the context-engine hypergraph itself; `tools/` (root) holds standalone non-domain utilities (migrate-edges, tracing-analyzer, dungeon-crawler, crane-cli). A PDF domain crate is a domain-store-style tool, so it belongs under `memory-api/`.

Following the `peek` pattern exactly, placement would be:
```
memory-api/crates/pdf-api/
memory-api/tools/cli/pdf-cli/
memory-api/tools/mcp/pdf-mcp/
```
Root [Cargo.toml](Cargo.toml) `members` would need three new entries added (alongside the existing peek/fs/compact-terminal rows), e.g.:
```

"memory-api/tools/cli/pdf-cli",
"memory-api/tools/mcp/pdf-mcp",
```
No other workspace file needs member edits — `memory-api/rule-targets.yaml`, viewer workspaces, and `context-stack/Cargo.toml` are unrelated unless a `pdf-viewer` frontend is later desired (not requested).

## D. Skill System Integration Requirements

Per [.agents/skills/README.md](.agents/skills/README.md):
- One folder per skill: `.agents/skills/pdf/SKILL.md` (or similar slug matching the folder name).
- **Required YAML frontmatter fields**: `name` (unique slug, matches folder) and `description` (the by-description loading trigger — must let an agent decide applicability from the description alone). Optional: `applyTo` (glob path-scoped activation).
- Actual usage in this repo (e.g. [rust-best-practices/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/rust-best-practices/SKILL.md)) also includes non-required extras: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata.author`/`metadata.version`, `allowed-tools` — these appear only on **vendored** skills reproducing upstream frontmatter, not required by the repo's own contract.
- Skills are **hand-owned and never generated** — explicitly forbidden to carry a `<!-- rule-api:file generated=true -->` header (that header belongs to rule-mcp-generated instructions/rule files, a different system). So a new `pdf` skill is authored directly as a plain markdown file, not through `rule-mcp`.
- Governing spec: `agents/skill-infrastructure` (`a9b7ef39-ace4-4a12-a171-80f54548fc65`) — should be checked/updated if the skill-authoring contract itself changes, but authoring a new skill instance doesn't require a spec change.
- After creation: add the skill's row to the Master Index table in [.agents/skills/README.md](.agents/skills/README.md) (hand-owned section since it'd wrap our own Rust CLI, not a vendored upstream skill).
- `skills-lock.json` only tracks **vendored** skills (source repo, `skillPath`, `computedHash`) — it is not touched for a hand-owned skill like this one.

## G. Open Design Questions (for a human to decide before implementation)

1. **Contract shape mismatch**: Should `pdf` follow the aspirational single-facade-crate-with-feature-gated-bins pattern in [WORKFLOW_TOOLS_DOMAIN_CRATE_CONTRACT.md](WORKFLOW_TOOLS_DOMAIN_CRATE_CONTRACT.md), or the three-separate-crates pattern every existing tool (peek, ticket, spec, fs, etc.) actually uses? 2. **Pure-Rust vs native-binding dependency policy**: is a C/C++ binding dependency (e.g. `pdfium-render`, if it depends on a bundled/linked pdfium binary) acceptable in this workspace, or is pure-Rust (`lopdf`, `pdf-extract`, `printpdf`) mandatory? 3. **typst as runtime dependency vs vendored/optional**: is `typst-cli` invoked as an external process, linked as a library, or excluded entirely? Markup→PDF creation is a materially different capability from programmatic PDF construction.

9. **Licensing**: several named crates' licenses are unverified; if any candidate is not MIT/Apache-2.0-compatible, that changes crate selection entirely.

## Design

Investigate (using whatever access is available — `cargo search`, `cargo info`, crates.io, docs.rs, lockfiles of other repos, or local knowledge) for each of: `lopdf`, `pdf-extract`, `printpdf`, and any other pure-Rust PDF crate found that has no C/C++ binding requirement (explicitly excluding `pdfium-render` and any wrapper around a native PDF renderer):

2. Maintenance status (last release date, open issue/PR velocity if determinable, whether it looks abandoned).
3. License (must resolve to MIT or Apache-2.0, or a compatible permissive license; reject anything GPL/AGPL or unclear).
4. Which of the six v1 capabilities it actually covers, concretely:

   - embedded image extraction
   - page operations (merge/split/reorder/delete)
   - metadata read/write
   - PDF creation (programmatic)

- [ ] A capability coverage matrix (crate x capability) is produced.
- [ ] A final crate selection decision is written back into this ticket's description (or a linked section) covering all six v1 capabilities, with no unresolved "TBD".

Manual review: the crate selection decision recorded in this ticket is reviewed against the license and pure-Rust constraints before T1 starts. No automated test applies to a research spike; validation is the presence of a complete, unambiguous decision record with no unresolved TBDs.

Follow the `peek-api` shape (`memory-api/crates/peek-api/src/lib.rs`): a single tagged serde request enum, e.g.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind")]
pub enum PdfRequest {
    ExtractText { path: PathBuf },
    ExtractImages { path: PathBuf, output_dir: PathBuf },
    Merge { inputs: Vec<PathBuf>, output: PathBuf, overwrite: bool },
    Split { path: PathBuf, output_dir: PathBuf },
    ReorderPages { path: PathBuf, output: PathBuf, order: Vec<usize>, overwrite: bool },
    DeletePages { path: PathBuf, output: PathBuf, pages: Vec<usize>, overwrite: bool },
    ReadMetadata { path: PathBuf },
    WriteMetadata { path: PathBuf, output: PathBuf, metadata: PdfMetadata, overwrite: bool },
    CreateProgrammatic { output: PathBuf, spec: PdfCreateSpec, overwrite: bool },
    CreateFromTypst { source: PathBuf, output: PathBuf, overwrite: bool },
}
```
(Field names/shape are illustrative; finalize field names to match whatever the T0-selected crates naturally expose, but the tagged-enum-of-operations structure itself is fixed by this ticket.)

A single dispatch function:
```rust
pub fn execute(root: &Path, request: &PdfRequest) -> Result<PdfResponse, PdfError>
```
`root` is the allowlisted confinement root (mirrors `fs-api`'s `root` parameter pattern in `mutation.rs`).

**Sandboxing**: every path in every request variant (input and output) must be validated with a `pdf-api`-local port of `validate_path_within_root` from `memory-api/crates/fs-api/src/security.rs` (either by depending on `fs-api` directly and reusing its function, or by copying the canonicalize-then-prefix-check logic into a local `pdf-api::security` module — prefer depending on `fs-api` directly if that does not create a circular/undesirable dependency; document whichever choice is made in this ticket's implementation).

**Write safety**: any operation that produces an output file must:
- Require an explicit `output` path in the request (no defaulting to overwriting the input).
- Reject the operation with a `PdfError` variant (e.g. `PdfError::OutputExists`) if `output` already exists and the request's `overwrite` field is not `true`.
- Only overwrite when `overwrite: true` is explicitly set.

`PdfError` (thiserror) must have distinct variants for: path escapes root, output exists without `overwrite`, input file not found, malformed/corrupt PDF, unsupported operation, and an underlying-crate error passthrough variant. Map errors to MCP `invalid_params` (user error: bad path, missing overwrite flag, bad page index) vs `internal_error` (corrupt PDF, unexpected crate failure) — the exact mapping ships in T7, but `PdfError` variants must be classifiable as user-error vs internal-error at that layer.

Do not implement PDF-format-specific logic bodies for text extraction, image extraction, merge/split, metadata, or creation in this ticket — those are stubbed (e.g. `todo!()` or minimal pass-through) and filled in by T3/T4/T5/T9. This ticket's scope is the request/response/error/dispatch/security skeleton, not full operation bodies. (If the T0-selected crates make a given operation trivial to implement immediately, doing so here is acceptable but not required.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single tagged serde request enum exists covering all six v1 capabilities (text extraction, image extraction, merge, split, page reorder/delete, metadata read+write, creation programmatic, creation via typst).
- [ ] A single `execute(root, request) -> Result<PdfResponse, PdfError>` dispatch function exists and routes every request variant.
- [ ] Every request variant containing a filesystem path is validated against `root` before any file I/O occurs, rejecting paths that escape the root (unit test proves a `../` or symlink-escape path is rejected).
- [ ] Any request variant that writes an output file returns `PdfError` when the output path exists and `overwrite` is not `true` (unit test proves this).
- [ ] The same request variant succeeds and overwrites when `overwrite: true` is set and the output already exists (unit test proves this).
- [ ] `PdfError` is a `thiserror`-derived enum with distinct variants distinguishing user error from internal error.
- [ ] `cargo build -p pdf-api` succeeds with the T0-selected PDF-processing dependencies added to `Cargo.toml`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p pdf-api` passes.

## Validation Plan

```bash
cargo build -p pdf-api
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib
```
Unit tests specifically covering: root-escape rejection, output-exists-without-overwrite rejection, and successful overwrite-with-flag path.

## Objective

Implement page/document-level operations: merge multiple PDFs into one, split a PDF into per-page (or per-range) output files, reorder/delete pages within a PDF, and read/write document metadata (title, author, subject, keywords, etc.).

## Target Files

- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/src/lib.rs` (or `src/pages.rs`, `src/metadata.rs` if split out) — implement `Merge`, `Split`, `ReorderPages`, `DeletePages`, `ReadMetadata`, `WriteMetadata` request variant bodies.
- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/tests/` — tests for each operation using small multi-page fixture PDFs.

## Design

Implement using the crate T0 selected for structural PDF editing (candidate: `lopdf`, to be confirmed by T0). All operations route through the T2 sandboxing + write-safety layer already in place — no new path-validation logic here.

- **Merge**: takes an ordered list of input PDF paths, produces one output PDF containing all pages in input order. Reject empty input list as a user error.
- **Split**: takes one input PDF and an output directory, produces one output file per page (or per contiguous range if the request shape from T2 supports ranges — confirm against the finalized `PdfRequest::Split` shape). Naming convention for split output files must be deterministic (e.g. `<original-stem>-page-<n>.pdf`), documented here once implemented.
- **ReorderPages / DeletePages**: takes an input path, an explicit `output` path, and a page index list; page indices are 0-based (or 1-based — pick one and document it consistently across the whole crate, including in the skill doc from T8). Out-of-range page indices are a user error, not a panic.
- **ReadMetadata**: returns whatever standard metadata fields the input PDF has set (title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, creation/mod dates) as an optional-field struct — absent fields are `None`, not empty-string.
- **WriteMetadata**: takes an input path, explicit `output` path, and a metadata struct with optional fields; only overwrites the fields provided (fields left `None` in the request preserve the existing value from the input document).

All output-producing operations enforce the copy-on-write / `overwrite` flag semantics from T2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Merge` combines N input PDFs into one output file with total page count equal to the sum of input page counts, in input order.
- [ ] `Merge` rejects an empty input list as a user error.
- [ ] `Split` produces one output file per page (or per range) with a documented, deterministic naming scheme.
- [ ] `ReorderPages` produces an output PDF with pages in the requested order; an out-of-range page index is rejected as a user error, not a panic.
- [ ] `DeletePages` produces an output PDF missing exactly the requested pages, with remaining pages preserved in original relative order.
- [ ] `ReadMetadata` returns `None` for unset fields and the correct value for fields that are set on a fixture PDF with known metadata.
- [ ] `WriteMetadata` updates only the fields provided in the request and preserves all other existing metadata and page content unchanged.
- [ ] All output-producing operations in this ticket refuse to overwrite an existing output path unless `overwrite: true` (reusing, not reimplementing, T2's enforcement).
- [ ] `cargo test -p pdf-api` passes including new tests for merge, split, reorder, delete, read-metadata, write-metadata.

## Validation Plan

```bash
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib merge
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib split
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib reorder
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib delete_pages
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib metadata
```
Use small multi-page fixture PDFs (2-5 pages) with known metadata checked into `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/tests/fixtures/`.

## Objective

Implement PDF creation in two modes: (a) a programmatic primitive using a pure-Rust PDF-generation crate (candidate: `printpdf`, to be confirmed by T0), and (b) an optional path that shells out to `typst-cli` when detected on PATH, producing PDF output directly from a typst source document, degrading gracefully with a clear error when `typst-cli` is not installed.

## Target Files

- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/src/lib.rs` (or `src/create.rs` if split out) — implement `CreateProgrammatic` and `CreateFromTypst` request variant bodies.
- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/tests/` — tests for both creation paths.

## Design

**Programmatic primitive (`CreateProgrammatic`)**: Accepts a minimal, crate-agnostic `PdfCreateSpec` (finalized once T0/T2 settle on the crate — expected to support at minimum: page size, and a list of text blocks with position and font size; image embedding in a created document is out of scope for this ticket — that is a separate concern from T9's image *extraction*). Produces a new PDF at the request's `output` path, subject to T2's copy-on-write/`overwrite` enforcement and sandboxing.

**Typst path (`CreateFromTypst`)**: Accepts a `source` path (a `.typst` file, itself subject to root confinement) and an `output` path. Detection: at request time, check whether `typst-cli` (or `typst`, depending on what the actual installed binary is named — confirm during implementation) is resolvable on `PATH` (e.g. via `which`/`Command::new("typst").arg("--version")` probe). If not found, return a `PdfError` variant (e.g. `PdfError::TypstNotFound`) with a clear, actionable message — do not panic, do not silently fall back to the programmatic primitive. If found, shell out via `std::process::Command` to compile the typst source to the requested output path, propagating typst's own error output into the `PdfError` on non-zero exit.

`typst-cli` must NOT be added as a `[dependencies]` or `[build-dependencies]` entry in `Cargo.toml` — it is a runtime-only, optional external tool. This must be explicit in code comments and in this ticket's validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CreateProgrammatic` produces a valid, openable PDF file containing the requested text content at the requested page size.
- [ ] `CreateProgrammatic` respects T2's copy-on-write/`overwrite` enforcement (refuses to clobber an existing output path without `overwrite: true`).
- [ ] `CreateFromTypst` detects `typst-cli` presence/absence on `PATH` at request time (not at build time).
- [ ] `CreateFromTypst` returns a clear, actionable `PdfError` (not a panic, not a generic I/O error) when `typst-cli` is absent.
- [ ] `CreateFromTypst` produces a valid output PDF when `typst-cli` is present and given valid typst source (test may be conditionally skipped in CI environments lacking `typst-cli`, but the skip must be explicit and logged, not silent).
- [ ] `typst-cli`/`typst` does not appear in `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` or `[build-dependencies]`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p pdf-api` passes (with the typst-present test conditionally skipped where `typst-cli` is unavailable).

## Validation Plan

```bash
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib create_programmatic
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib create_from_typst
```
The typst-path test must explicitly detect `typst-cli` availability in the test itself and report a skip (not a silent pass) when unavailable, per this ticket's acceptance criteria.

## Objective

Wire the `pdf-mcp` binary transport following the canonical named-tool MCP pattern from `memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/src/server.rs`, exposing every `pdf-api` operation as a named MCP tool.

## Target Files

- `memory-api/crates/pdf/src/bin/pdf-mcp.rs`
- `memory-api/crates/pdf/Cargo.toml` (confirm `mcp` feature deps: `rmcp`, `schemars`, `serde`, `serde_json` alongside `transport-harness`)

## Design

Mirror `memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/src/server.rs` exactly in structure:

- One `#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] pub struct <Op>Input` per operation (e.g. `PdfExtractTextInput`, `PdfMergeInput`, `PdfSplitInput`, `PdfReorderPagesInput`, `PdfDeletePagesInput`, `PdfReadMetadataInput`, `PdfWriteMetadataInput`, `PdfCreateInput`, `PdfCreateFromTypstInput`, `PdfExtractImagesInput`), each carrying whatever fields the corresponding `PdfRequest` variant needs, plus a `root: String` (or `PathBuf`) confinement field on every input (mirroring how `fs-mcp`-family tools take `root` — confirm the exact convention used by an existing root-confined MCP tool in this repo, e.g. `mcp_fs-mcp_fs_list_dir`'s `root` parameter, and match it).
- `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct PdfServer { tool_router: ToolRouter<Self> }` with `pub fn new() -> Self`.
- A `json_result<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> Result<CallToolResult, McpError>` helper identical in shape to peek-mcp's.
- An error-mapper converting `PdfError` variants to `McpError`: user-error variants (bad path, root escape, missing overwrite flag, out-of-range page index, file not found) map to `McpError::invalid_params`; everything else (corrupt PDF, unexpected crate failure, typst-cli process failure) maps to `McpError::internal_error`.
- `#[tool_router] impl PdfServer` with one `#[tool(name = "...", description = "...")] async fn` per operation, each taking `Parameters<XInput>`, calling `pdf_api::execute`, and returning via `json_result`/the error mapper.
- `#[tool_handler] impl ServerHandler for PdfServer` setting `server_info` from `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")`/`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, an `instructions` string describing the PDF toolset and pointing agents to prefer these named tools over `pdf-cli`, and `ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build()`.
- `pdf-mcp.rs`'s `main` calls a `run_mcp_server()`-equivalent that does `PdfServer::new().serve(stdio()).await?.waiting().await?;` per the peek-mcp precedent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pdf-mcp` exposes one named tool per `pdf-api` operation (text extraction, image extraction, merge, split, reorder, delete, read-metadata, write-metadata, create-programmatic, create-from-typst).
- [ ] Every tool input struct includes an explicit confinement root field; no tool defaults or omits it.
- [ ] Every output-producing tool input includes an explicit `output` path and `overwrite` flag mirroring T2's write-safety contract.
- [ ] `PdfError` user-error variants map to `McpError::invalid_params`; internal/unexpected failures map to `McpError::internal_error` (unit or integration test confirms at least one case of each mapping).
- [ ] `server_info` reports the correct package name/version and an `instructions` string mentioning PDF operations.
- [ ] `cargo build -p pdf --features mcp` succeeds and produces a working `pdf-mcp` binary that starts an MCP stdio server.
- [ ] Tool-router registration includes all operations (no operation from `PdfRequest` is left unexposed as an MCP tool, except none are expected to be withheld — confirm 1:1 coverage).

## Validation Plan

```bash
cargo build -p pdf --features mcp
```
Manual MCP client smoke test (e.g. via an MCP inspector or a short-lived stdio session) calling the extract-text tool against a T3 fixture and confirming the expected text is returned, plus one deliberate error case (bad root) confirming `invalid_params` is returned rather than a crash.

## Objective

Implement embedded image extraction from PDFs: given a PDF, extract each embedded raster image to a file in an output directory. Sequenced last so it can be cut from v1 without blocking any other capability.

## Target Files

- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/src/lib.rs` (or `src/images.rs` if split out) — implement the `ExtractImages` request variant body.
- `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/tests/` — tests using a fixture PDF containing at least one embedded raster image.
- `memory-api/crates/pdf/src/bin/pdf-cli.rs` — add the `extract-images` subcommand (already scaffolded as a placeholder in T6; fill in behavior here).
- `memory-api/crates/pdf/src/bin/pdf-mcp.rs` — add the `extract_images` named tool (already scaffolded as a placeholder in T7; fill in behavior here).

## Design

Implement using whatever crate T0 identified as covering image extraction (may be the same structural crate used for merge/split/metadata, e.g. `lopdf`'s embedded-XObject image stream access, or may require an additional crate — confirm against T0's final findings). If T0 concluded no adequate pure-Rust crate exists for this capability, this ticket's scope narrows to: implement the best-effort subset that is achievable (e.g. only the most common image encodings present in embedded PDF streams), explicitly documenting any image encoding left unsupported, rather than blocking the ticket entirely — the epic already treats this capability as cuttable/best-effort-last.

Each extracted image is written to the request's `output_dir` (an explicit path, subject to T2's root confinement) with a deterministic filename (e.g. `<original-stem>-image-<n>.<ext>`, extension matching the detected image encoding). Extraction does not overwrite the source PDF; it only writes new files into `output_dir`, so the copy-on-write semantics here are: reject if any target image filename already exists in `output_dir` unless `overwrite: true`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ExtractImages` extracts at least one embedded image from a fixture PDF known to contain an embedded raster image, writing it to the requested output directory with a deterministic filename.

- [ ] `ExtractImages` on a PDF with no embedded images returns success with zero extracted files, not an error.
- [ ] `ExtractImages` refuses to overwrite an existing output filename in `output_dir` unless `overwrite: true`, consistent with T2's write-safety contract.
- [ ] Any image encoding explicitly unsupported by the T0-selected crate(s) is documented in this ticket's description (updated during implementation) rather than causing a silent empty/wrong result.
- [ ] `pdf-cli extract-images` and the `pdf-mcp` `extract_images` tool both invoke this implementation and are covered by at least one manual invocation against a fixture.
- [ ] `cargo test -p pdf-api` passes including the new image-extraction tests.
- [ ] This ticket has no dependent tickets in the `depends_on` graph (confirmed via `mcp_ticket-mcp_list_edges` after creation).

## Validation Plan

```bash
cargo test -p pdf-api --lib extract_images
./target/debug/pdf-cli extract-images --root <fixtures-dir> --output-dir <fixtures-dir>/out-images <fixtures-dir>/sample-with-image.pdf
```

# Epic: PDF Domain Capability

## Objective

Add a `pdf` domain to the repository so agents can work with PDF files through
MCP named tools, backed by a pure-Rust implementation, plus a hand-authored
skill that teaches agents when and how to use it.

## Capabilities (v1)

| # | Capability | Ticket |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Extract text from a PDF | T3 |
| 2 | Merge multiple PDFs into one | T4 |
| 3 | Split a PDF into page ranges / single pages | T4 |
| 4 | Edit pages (reorder, delete, rotate) and read/write document metadata | T4 |
| 5 | Create a new PDF (programmatic primitive + optional typst path) | T5 |
| 6 | Extract embedded raster images | T9 (cuttable) |

## Locked Decisions

These were resolved with the user before the track was authored. Do not re-open
them during implementation; if implementation evidence contradicts one, stop and
escalate rather than silently deviating.

1. **Crate shape — follow the written contract, not the peek precedent.**
   `WORKFLOW_TOOLS_DOMAIN_CRATE_CONTRACT.md` governs. An internal `pdf-api`
   crate holds types/logic/errors. A public facade crate `pdf` re-exports
   `pdf-api` from `src/lib.rs` and declares `[[bin]]` targets
   `pdf-cli` and `pdf-mcp`, each gated by a cargo feature (`cli`, `mcp`) that
   also gates the shared `transport-harness` dependency.
   `memory-api/crates/ticket/Cargo.toml` is the in-repo crate that already
   implements this exact shape and is the closest copy target.
2. **Placement.** `memory-api/crates/pdf-api/` and `memory-api/crates/pdf/`,
   both registered in the ROOT `Cargo.toml` `members` list.
3. **Pure Rust only.** `lopdf` / `pdf-extract` / `printpdf` family. No
   `pdfium-render`, no C/C++ bindings — not even behind an optional feature.
   Rationale: reproducible builds and cross-platform CI without a native
   toolchain.
4. **Creation has two modes.** A programmatic primitive, plus an optional path
   that shells out to `typst-cli` **only when it is detected on PATH**. typst is
   not a build dependency; absence must produce a clear, actionable error, never
   a panic or a silent fallback.
5. **Write safety.** Copy-on-write by default: an explicit output path is
   required. In-place overwrite is permitted only when the request carries an
   explicit `overwrite: true`. Never silently clobber an existing file.
   `memory-api/crates/fs-api/src/mutation.rs` already implements this exact
   `overwrite` semantic and is the precedent to mirror.
6. **Sandboxing.** All reads and writes are confined to an allowlisted root,
   reusing `fs-api::security::validate_path_within_root` in
   `memory-api/crates/fs-api/src/security.rs`. That function canonicalizes both
   path and root to defeat symlink/junction escapes, and handles
   not-yet-existing destination paths by canonicalizing the parent. There is no
   opt-out.
7. **Image extraction is sequenced last** (T9) and nothing may depend on it, so
   it can be cut without blocking the rest of the track.
8. **No crate facts are verified.** The session that produced this track had no
   web access. No crate version, API signature, license, or feature flag has
   been confirmed. T0 is a bounded verification spike that must resolve this
   before any dependency is added. Downstream tickets therefore state
   acceptance criteria **behaviorally**, not in terms of specific upstream APIs.
9. **Skill is hand-authored.** `.agents/skills/pdf/SKILL.md`, plain markdown,
   NOT rule-mcp generated, and must not carry a `rule-api:file generated=true`
   header. It directs agents to the `pdf-mcp` named tools and documents
   `pdf-cli` as the fallback, mirroring how `peek` is documented.
10. **HTTP transport is out of scope for v1.** Tracked as a separate backlog
    follow-up ticket, not on the v1 critical path.

## Non-Goals

- No `pdf-http` bin in v1.
- No native/C++ bindings.
- No viewer or frontend crate.
- No OCR, no scanned-document text recovery.
- No PDF form filling, signing, or encryption in v1.

## Architecture

Follows the `peek-api` shape for the API crate:

- A tagged serde request enum (`#[serde(tag = "kind")]`) covering every
  operation, response types, and a `PdfError` (`thiserror`) enum.
- One `execute(&PdfRequest) -> Result<PdfResponse, PdfError>` dispatch entry.
- All bounding, validation, and safety enforcement live in `pdf-api`. Transport
  layers stay thin.

MCP surface follows `memory-api/tools/mcp/peek-mcp/src/server.rs`: one
`#[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]` input struct per named tool, a
`ToolRouter`-carrying server struct, a `json_result` helper, and an error mapper
sending user errors to `McpError::invalid_params` and everything else to
`internal_error`.

## Sequencing

T0 → T1 → T2 → {T3, T4, T5} → T6 → T7 → T8, with T9 last and unblocking nothing.

## Risk Register

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Candidate crates may not actually cover the capabilities | T0 spike gates all dependency choices |
| A candidate crate may carry an incompatible license | T0 must confirm MIT/Apache-2.0 compatibility |
| Image extraction may need a decoder stack we do not want | T9 is sequenced last and is cuttable |
| Agent-invoked file writes are a data-loss vector | Decisions 5 + 6, enforced centrally in T2 |

# T6: `pdf-cli` Transport

## Objective

Wire the `pdf-cli` binary so every `pdf-api` operation is reachable from the
command line. The CLI is a thin adapter — no PDF logic lives here.

## Files

- `memory-api/crates/pdf/src/bin/pdf-cli.rs` (replace T1 stub)
- `memory-api/crates/pdf/tests/cli.rs` (new)

## Design

Use `transport-harness` for shared CLI scaffolding, gated by the `cli` feature.
`memory-api/crates/ticket/src/bin/ticket-cli.rs` is the in-repo reference for
how the harness is consumed; follow it rather than hand-rolling arg parsing
conventions.

### Subcommands

One per `pdf-api` operation:

```
pdf-cli extract-text <input> [--pages <range>] [--max-chars <n>]
pdf-cli merge <inputs...> --output <path> [--overwrite]
pdf-cli split <input> --output-dir <dir> [--pages <ranges>] [--overwrite]
pdf-cli edit-pages <input> --output <path> [--delete <r>] [--reorder <spec>] [--rotate <spec>] [--overwrite]
pdf-cli metadata get <input>
pdf-cli metadata set <input> --output <path> [--title ...] [--author ...] [--overwrite]
pdf-cli create --mode <programmatic|typst> ... --output <path> [--overwrite]
pdf-cli extract-images <input> --output-dir <dir> [--overwrite]   # gated on T9
```

### Sandbox root

Every invocation needs a root. Provide `--root <path>` with a documented default
(current working directory is the reasonable default for a CLI). Document
clearly that the root is a safety boundary, not a convenience.

### Output format

Support `--json` and, per the repo's compact-output guidance, `--toon` for
machine-readable output, with human-readable as the default. `peek-api` already
depends on `toon-format`; follow that precedent rather than hand-rolling.

### Exit codes

- 0 success.
- Distinct non-zero code for user errors vs internal errors, driven by
  `PdfError::is_user_error()` from T2. Errors go to stderr; machine-readable
  output stays clean on stdout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `pdf-api` operation has a subcommand.
- [ ] `--help` documents every subcommand and flag, including that `--root` is a
      security boundary.
- [ ] `--json` and `--toon` produce valid parseable output; human output is the
      default.
- [ ] User errors exit with a distinct code from internal errors.
- [ ] Errors go to stderr; stdout stays clean in machine-readable modes.
- [ ] `--overwrite` is required to clobber; without it the CLI refuses and says
      so.
- [ ] A path outside `--root` is refused.
- [ ] The binary only builds under `--features cli`.
- [ ] No PDF logic in the CLI — it constructs a `PdfRequest` and calls
      `execute()`.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p pdf --features cli
cargo run -p pdf --features cli --bin pdf-cli -- --help
```

## Depends On

T3, T4, T5.

**Acceptance-criteria risk, given B's findings:**
- I did not read every ticket's literal AC text (out of the bounded-research budget and because the epic/spec already state ACs are written *behaviorally*, not against specific APIs — confirmed in the epic body: *"Downstream acceptance criteria are written behaviorally, not in terms of specific upstream APIs."*). Given that framing, my B-section findings do **not** surface a literal AC contradiction — they surface **assumptions T0 still needs to close**, not broken tickets. The two AC-relevant risks worth flagging explicitly for T0's findings section:
  - T5's "programmatic creation primitive" AC should not silently assume a base-14/no-asset text path is available in `printpdf` — if it isn't, T5 needs to either ship a bundled font (license-compatible, e.g. a permissively licensed open font) or evaluate `krilla` instead.
  - T9 (and arguably T0) needs an explicit finding on CCITTFaxDecode/JPXDecode coverage before T9's scope is finalized — I could not confirm or deny this from the outside.

**R1–R10 capabilities with no fully-confirmed pure-Rust crate today:**
- R1.7 (image extraction, T9) — partially open. FlateDecode/DCTDecode plausible via `lopdf`+`image`; CCITTFax/JPX genuinely unconfirmed. Fallback per locked decision 7: cut and report (R10 already anticipates "unsupported images are skipped and reported, never emitted corrupt" — this is the right shape for whatever gap exists).
- Everything else in R1 (extract, merge, split, edit, metadata, create) has at least one actively-maintained pure-Rust crate with directly relevant, README-demonstrated capability (`lopdf` for structure/merge, `pdf-extract` for text, `printpdf`/`krilla` for creation).

**What's missing from the plan entirely — my assessment of each item you asked about:**
- **Encrypted/password-protected PDF handling** — **warrants a ticket-level decision, not silence.** This is the one place my research materially changes the picture: `lopdf` already auto-detects encryption and auto-decrypts empty-password PDFs, which is a real, common case (many "protected" PDFs use permission-only encryption with an empty user password). Right now, an agent handing `pdf-mcp` a real-world encrypted PDF that isn't empty-password-protected will get *some* failure from `lopdf`, but the current plan has no ticket defining what error that should surface as, and no ticket exploits the empty-password case that already works for free. Recommendation: **do not add a "handle encryption" feature ticket** (that would reopen Non-Goal 6, correctly listed as out of scope) — instead, **add a small, explicit AC to T2 or T3/T4**: detect `is_encrypted()` on load; if `encryption_state` after lopdf's own attempt indicates it's still locked, return a distinct, actionable `PdfError` variant (e.g. `EncryptedUnsupported`) rather than a generic parse failure. This is a few hours of work, not a new capability, and prevents a confusing error message being the actual behavior by accident.
- **Form-field (AcroForm) read/fill** — **spec non-goal is correct, no change needed.** Already explicitly listed as a non-goal in both the spec and epic ("No PDF form filling... in v1"). Anthropic's own skill shows this is a substantial, script-heavy feature (bounding-box-to-image round-trip, JSON field schemas) — appropriately out of scope for v1, and I found nothing that argues for pulling it back in.
- **Linearization / repair of malformed PDFs** — **currently unaddressed, and I think it deserves a one-line spec non-goal rather than a ticket.** Real-world PDFs are frequently mildly malformed (bad xref offsets, missing `EOF` markers), and `lopdf`'s issue tracker (82 open issues — I did not read individual issues, so this is inference from count alone, not verified content) plausibly includes such reports. I don't have evidence this needs *implementation* work — I have evidence it's a real class of input that will produce `PdfError` failures. Recommendation: add a short Non-Goal line to the spec: *"No repair/recovery of malformed or non-conformant PDF structure; such inputs surface as a normal `PdfError`."* This is documentation, not a ticket.
- **PDF/A conformance** — **nothing needed.** No R1 requirement implies conformance output, and there's no evidence any user-facing need exists. Recommend leaving entirely unaddressed (not even a non-goal line) unless a future capability specifically requires archival conformance.
